title: A wind-down routine for a good night's sleep
examples: What is a good bedtime routine?
Why should I turn off screens before bed?
How can I fall asleep faster?

explain.say: Imagine trying to stop a racing car in one second: screech! Your brain is the same at bedtime; it needs time to slow down. Look at the checklist on the board. Step one: screens off, about an hour before bed.

faq.q: Why should I turn off screens before bed?
faq.a: Bright screens and exciting games or videos keep your brain awake, and screen light can delay your sleepy chemical, melatonin. A calm hour without screens helps you fall asleep.
asks: Is it bad to use a phone in bed?

faq.q: Why does darkness help me sleep?
faq.a: When it gets dark, a tiny gland in your brain makes melatonin, a chemical that makes you feel sleepy. Light, even from a screen, slows it down.
asks: Why do I sleep better in the dark?

faq.q: Why should I go to bed at the same time?
faq.a: Your body has an inner clock. Going to bed and waking at similar times each day sets the clock, so you feel sleepy at bedtime and fresher in the morning.

faq.q: What if I cannot fall asleep?
faq.a: Stay calm and try slow belly breathing or imagining a peaceful place. If you often lie awake for a long time, tell a grown-up; they may ask a doctor for advice.
asks: How can I fall asleep faster?

faq.q: What if I wake up from a bad dream?
faq.a: Bad dreams are normal and are not real. Take slow breaths, hug a soft toy, and tell a grown-up if you need comfort.
asks: What do I do after a nightmare?

facts: Melatonin, the body's sleepy chemical, is made by a tiny gland in the brain called the pineal gland, mostly when it is dark.
Light from screens can delay the release of melatonin and make it harder to fall asleep.
